excluded_original_source_records.title: Detecting acute pain signals from human EEG
excluded_original_source_records.authors: G Sun, Z Wen, D Ok, L Doan, J Wang, Z S Chen et al.

excluded_original_source_records.feature_definition: Unsupervised state-space detector using localized ROI EEG to detect onset of acute pain, compared with SVM.
excluded_original_source_records.prediction_rationale: An onset detector estimates pain occurrence from brain activity, complementary to rating-level prediction.
excluded_original_source_records.verified_result_metric: Paper reports feasibility across two EEG datasets and cross-subject/cross-modality tests versus SVM; no numeric accuracy captured in the inspected abstract/source excerpts.
excluded_original_source_records.prediction_target: Presence/onset of acute experimentally induced pain, not continuous subjective rating.
excluded_original_source_records.validation_design: Two EEG datasets with cross-subject and cross-modality evaluation; source localization and sequential modeling.
excluded_original_source_records.data_evidence: The primary paper links to public OSF Brain mediators of pain study data; the OSF record describes BrainVision EEG and perception-condition numeric ratings for 60 painful stimuli/condition at three intensity levels. This verifies public EEG and ratings, not that every analysis subset is identical.
excluded_original_source_records.relevance_limitations: Published method depends on source localization and temporal context; the linked EEG is 1000-Hz/65-channel in the cited dataset description, unlike the target 128-Hz sparse montage. Onset detection is not a pain-intensity regression target.
excluded_original_source_records.review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations

excluded_original_source_records.title: Selective and replicable neuroimaging-based indicators of pain discriminability
excluded_original_source_records.authors: Zhang et al.
excluded_original_source_records.feature_family: Evoked-potential response amplitude and latency; pain AUC
excluded_original_source_records.feature_definition: Differences in N2/P2 peak amplitude and latency; signal-detection-theory AUC operationalizes an individual’s pain discriminability.
excluded_original_source_records.prediction_rationale: Inference: evoked EEG response features may estimate how sensitively an individual distinguishes pain intensity, not moment-to-moment pain itself.
excluded_original_source_records.verified_result_metric: LASSO-predicted AUC correlated with measured pain AUC: Pearson r=0.536 in Dataset 1 and r=0.423 in Dataset 2 (both p<0.0001). These are correlations, not R²/accuracy.
excluded_original_source_records.prediction_target: Individual pain-intensity discriminability (AUC).
excluded_original_source_records.validation_design: Three EEG cohorts (N=114,111,141); exploratory Dataset 1 and replication in Datasets 2/3; pain-selectivity assessed against non-pain sensory modalities.
excluded_original_source_records.data_evidence: Linked EEG dataset paper lists raw BIDS records including ds005292; this specific data page describes trialwise pain ratings.
excluded_original_source_records.relevance_limitations: Peak-based, stimulus-locked feature design requires event-aligned epochs and broad scalp electrodes; article’s AUC target is not a pain rating forecast and its evidence is not based on 5-s resting windows.
excluded_original_source_records.review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations

excluded_original_source_records.title: Chronic neuropathic pain: EEG data in eyes open and eyes closed with painDETECT and brief pain inventory reports
excluded_original_source_records.authors: Daniela M. Zolezzi, Norberto E. Naal-Ruiz, Luz María Alonso-Valerdi, David I. Ibarra-Zarate
excluded_original_source_records.feature_family: Public resting EEG resource for candidate PAC, phase connectivity and feature-stability analyses
excluded_original_source_records.feature_definition: Raw 250-Hz EEG from 36 chronic neuropathic-pain patients (5-min eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions) with BPI and painDETECT questionnaires; paper reports bandwidth 0.1–100 Hz.
excluded_original_source_records.prediction_rationale: Could test whether within-session phase/PAC summaries carry information about patient questionnaire pain scores; this is a proposed reanalysis, not a result of the data descriptor.
excluded_original_source_records.verified_result_metric: Not applicable (dataset item; no prediction result claimed).
excluded_original_source_records.prediction_target: Proposed patient-level BPI/painDETECT severity or questionnaire-defined pain features
excluded_original_source_records.validation_design: Dataset includes 36 patients; analyses need subject-level splits to avoid window-level leakage and independent validation before clinical claims.
excluded_original_source_records.data_evidence: The data article links Mendeley repository versions and identifies raw electrophysiological signals plus questionnaire/demographic files; repository metadata identifies original data and files.
excluded_original_source_records.relevance_limitations: Resting state, not stimulus-locked pain; only 36 patients; five-second window labels would replicate a subject’s fixed clinical scores and are not independent. excluded_original_source_records.review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations

excluded_original_source_records.title: EEG frequency band analysis in chronic neuropathic pain: A linear and nonlinear approach to classify pain severity
excluded_original_source_records.authors: Daniela M. Zolezzi; Luz María Alonso-Valerdi; David I. Ibarra-Zarate
excluded_original_source_records.feature_family: Approximate entropy (ApEn) and absolute EEG band power
excluded_original_source_records.feature_definition: ApEn (pattern-based signal irregularity) and absolute power estimated in delta, theta, alpha, beta and gamma bands at 22 scalp electrodes, using one-minute segments; chronic neuropathic pain severity grouped from Brief Pain Inventory ratings.
excluded_original_source_records.prediction_rationale: Authors tested whether nonlinear EEG signal dynamics/strength features separate pain severity groups better than absolute band power. The result is group differentiation rather than a validated out-of-sample pain predictor.
excluded_original_source_records.verified_result_metric: Paper reports ApEn group differences in most bands and conditions (p <= 0.0001) and notable clustering of pain groups using theta-, alpha- and beta-band ApEn. This is inferential/group-separation evidence, not verified held-out accuracy, correlation or R².
excluded_original_source_records.prediction_target: Low/moderate/high chronic neuropathic pain severity from Brief Pain Inventory; no prospective prediction endpoint.
excluded_original_source_records.validation_design: Cross-sectional feature comparison in 36 chronic neuropathic pain participants; 13-person healthy-control EEG database used as reference. Features derived from 10 one-minute observations per patient; Kruskal-Wallis/Dunn tests and unsupervised clustering described. No independent cohort or subject-held-out predictive validation verified.
excluded_original_source_records.open_access_status: Open-access article page/full text at ScienceDirect; article page identifies Creative Commons access.
excluded_original_source_records.data_evidence: Paper states its 36-patient database is publicly available; the linked Mendeley v4 page offers a public 529 MB download with individual patient .gdf recordings, demographics/questionnaires and channel labels. The companion data descriptor confirms these are raw electrophysiological recordings (250 Hz, 22 channels) paired with BPI/painDETECT reports. The 13 control participants come from a separate database; do not imply they are all contained in Mendeley dataset yj52xrfgtz. Access-review detail: public raw EEG verified
excluded_original_source_records.relevance_limitations: Relevant original pain-severity EEG analysis with public raw signals and central C3/Cz/C4 leads. However, its 1-min feature segments, 250-Hz 0.1–100-Hz acquisition and broad montage differ from 5-s, 128-Hz, 1–40-Hz workflows. BPI-derived groups and within-sample clustering do not prove calibrated individual pain prediction. It shares the Zolezzi cohort with the 2024 Ryu and Barbosa papers and the 2023 dataset descriptor; cohort reuse is not independent replication.
excluded_original_source_records.review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations

excluded_original_source_records.feature_definition: Gamma response prevalence, magnitude, and repeatability following noxious pain and innocuous touch stimulation.
excluded_original_source_records.prediction_rationale: Characterizes whether pain-related gamma features are stable enough to function as individual biomarkers.
excluded_original_source_records.verified_result_metric: Paper reports marked between-person variability and individual stability in one dataset, with gamma responses evident only in a subset; no pain-rating prediction accuracy verified.
excluded_original_source_records.prediction_target: Pain-evoked response reproducibility/individual trait, not a validated rating predictor.
excluded_original_source_records.validation_design: Two EEG datasets; 48-person pain/touch dataset linked to public OSF and a repeated-session dataset; study assesses repeatability and variability.
excluded_original_source_records.data_evidence: Paper links the 48-participant pain/touch EEG dataset to OSF jw8rv; article methods include pain ratings. This repository is for this gamma-stability dataset, not Nickel et al. 2017 tonic heat.
excluded_original_source_records.relevance_limitations: Gamma frequencies above 40 Hz are removed by the target filter and most are above 64-Hz Nyquist. Gamma response variability cautions against assuming this feature is universal.
excluded_original_source_records.review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations

excluded_original_source_records.title: Resting-state electroencephalography delta and theta bands as compensatory oscillations in chronic neuropathic pain: a secondary data analysis
excluded_original_source_records.authors: Sara Pinto Barbosa; Ygor Nascimento Junqueira; Milena Apetito Akamatsu; Lucas Murrins Marques; Adriano Teixeira; Matheus Lobo; Mohamed H Mahmoud; Walid E Omer; Kevin Pacheco-Barrios; Felipe Fregni
excluded_original_source_records.feature_family: Relative EEG band power (delta, theta, alpha, beta and sub-bands)
excluded_original_source_records.feature_definition: Resting eyes-closed relative power calculated with FFT from 5-second windows with 50% overlap; regional central, frontal and parietal power features analyzed against BPI pain intensity and interference outcomes.
excluded_original_source_records.prediction_rationale: The secondary analysis asks whether resting EEG spectral signal strength relates to pain severity/interference in neuropathic pain. Findings are associations from a small cross-sectional sample, not a validated forecast.
excluded_original_source_records.verified_result_metric: Authors report no significant multivariate model for pain during EEG or most interference outcomes; the model for average pain intensity over the prior four weeks and a separate mood-interference model were significant. Authors describe central alpha as associated with higher pain and central delta with lower pain. No independent-validation performance metric was verified.
excluded_original_source_records.prediction_target: Average pain intensity in the previous four weeks and BPI pain-interference outcomes; pain during EEG was also analyzed.
excluded_original_source_records.validation_design: Secondary cross-sectional analysis of 36 chronic neuropathic-pain participants from Zolezzi et al. 2023. excluded_original_source_records.data_evidence: The article identifies the sample as the public Zolezzi 2023 dataset, states the used data were provided by the original authors and are available in a publicly accessible database, and uses 36 patient EEG/BPI records. Mendeley v4 provides raw patient .gdf EEG and questionnaire files. Same participant cohort as Zolezzi 2023 and Ryu 2024; not a new cohort. Access-review detail: public raw EEG verified
excluded_original_source_records.relevance_limitations: The paper uses 5-s windows, but these are overlapping derived observations from 36 participants with person-level pain questionnaires; window count does not create independent participants. Association and regression are not held-out prediction; regional results and outcome coding need replication.

excluded_original_source_records.feature_definition: Cross-frequency coupling between low-frequency phase and higher-frequency amplitude at Fp1/Fp2; left-right asymmetry features.
excluded_original_source_records.prediction_rationale: PAC/asymmetry may capture chronic pain severity-related nonstationary interactions missed by band power; this rationale is directly tested by the paper’s correlations and regression models.
excluded_original_source_records.verified_result_metric: Reported r: beta-power asymmetry −0.375; gamma-power asymmetry −0.433; low-beta-to-low-gamma coupling −0.397. Best polynomial-kernel SVR R²=0.655; no external validation verified.
excluded_original_source_records.prediction_target: Patient-level chronic neuropathic pain intensity from clinical ratings
